name: JBT Marel Corporation

events.what: Completed JBT and Marel combination; board expanded 7 to 10 (Gronfeldt, Gudmundsson, Masson, Savage), C. Maury Devine resigned. Outside the 18 month window (21 months old)
events.who: Arni Sigurdsson (Marel CEO) appointed President; Brian Deck remains CEO

events.what: Investor Day 2026: next-gen strategy, 2028 targets (5% to 7% organic revenue CAGR, 20% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2028, 55% to 60% FCF conversion, $150M run-rate cost synergies by end of 2027)
events.who: Brian Deck, Matthew Meister, Arni Sigurdsson

statements.quote: The compound annual organic growth rate of 5%-7%, Adjusted EBITDA margin in 2028 of 20%.
statements.speaker: Matthew Meister

statements.quote: Based on that success and the actions that we've taken, we're very confident in our ability to remain on track to deliver that run-rate of $150 million in savings by the end of 2027. It's a key contributor to our expectation of delivering over 400 basis points improvement in margins by 2028.
statements.speaker: Matthew Meister

statements.quote: This pool of opportunities enhances confidence in our ability to deliver our profitable growth objectives and our target of 20% adjusted EBITDA margins in 2028.
statements.speaker: Brian Deck
statements.doc_title: JBT Marel Corporation Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), margins in percent, 4 EBITDA brokers. FY2028 consensus EBITDA ($736M) sits below FY2027 ($764M), likely a thin broker set; using FY2027 consensus 18.09% the gap to 20% is still 191 bps. current_level_pct 15.81 = FY2025 VA actual EBITDA $600.4M on $3,798.2M revenue (data_compute); Investor Day framed over 400 bps improvement by 2028.

evidence_of_progress.note: Company-reported adjusted EBITDA margin: Q1 2026 15.2%, +210 bps yoy (doc 176563, CFO snippet); Q2 2026 17.1% vs 16.7%, +40 bps (8-K 0001628280-26-051894 EX-99.1), and Q2 included $17M of IEEPA tariff refunds partly offset by $4M prior-year tariff expense and $5M accelerated LTI. Prepared Food and Beverage segment margin missed on footprint moves. Full year 2026 guide 17.0% to 17.5% (+145 bps at midpoint) maintained; synergies $43M realized in 2025 with $85M exit run-rate.

verdict: Best numeric framing of the three (20% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2028 plus $150M synergy run-rate by end 2027, repeated by CFO, President and CEO) against consensus about 300 bps short and the stock at the bottom of its EV/EBITDA range, but the Marel close (2025-01-02) is 3 months outside the catalyst window, leadership is unchanged, and at about 17% margin it is not a low-margin business, so it scores on framing rather than as a fresh GXO-style reset; borderline on the stale-catalyst disqualifier.
open_questions: Is the FY2028 consensus dip below FY2027 real or a 4-broker artifact, and where do the brokers who model 2028 sit versus 20%?
How much of the 2026 margin step is one-off (Q2 IEEPA tariff refunds) versus synergy and footprint savings, given Prepared Food and Beverage margins missed?
Without a leadership change, what would make the street underwrite 20% before 2028 results show it (synergy run-rate updates, PFB margin recovery)?
